name: STXBP1-related Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy (DEE4)

criteria.description: Presence of a heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in STXBP1 gene (confirmed by molecular genetic testing)
Onset of epilepsy (seizures) within the first year of life, typically before 12 months
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability, present from infancy
Exclusion of acquired or metabolic causes of encephalopathy
Presence of movement disorder (e.g., ataxia, dystonia, tremor)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met. Minor criteria are supportive but not required.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by molecular genetic testing. Clinical presentation is variable but typically includes early-onset epilepsy and developmental delay.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early-onset epileptic encephalopathy (seizures within first year)

laboratory: Normal or nonspecific metabolic and genetic screening except for STXBP1 variant
imaging: Brain MRI may be normal or show mild cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
genetic: Heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in STXBP1
other: EEG: Suppression-burst pattern or multifocal epileptiform discharges, especially in early infancy

distinguishingFeatures: KCNQ2 mutations affect potassium channels, not synaptic vesicle release
KCNQ2-DEE often presents with neonatal seizures and less prominent movement disorders
SCN2A-DEE may have later onset and different seizure types
CDKL5 mutations cause early-onset seizures, but often with Rett-like features and more severe cortical visual impairment

redFlags: Seizure onset in the first year of life with severe developmental delay
Movement disorder in a child with early-onset epilepsy
references: Stamberger H, et al. STXBP1 encephalopathy: A neurodevelopmental disorder including epilepsy. Neurology. 2016;86(10):954-962.
OMIM #612164: STXBP1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 4.
commonPitfalls: Assuming all early-onset epilepsies are due to metabolic causes without genetic testing
Missing the diagnosis in children with mild or atypical presentations
Overlooking movement disorders as part of the phenotype
Confusing with other DEEs based solely on seizure type
Failure to exclude acquired causes before genetic testing

extendedDiscriminators.feature: STXBP1-DEE has more prominent movement disorders and synaptic vesicle release dysfunction
STXBP1-DEE typically presents earlier and with different EEG patterns
STXBP1-DEE lacks Rett-like features and severe cortical visual impairment
STXBP1-DEE is genetic, not associated with perinatal insult
STXBP1-DEE has normal metabolic workup except for genetic findings

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of pathogenic or likely pathogenic STXBP1 variant on genetic testing
Identification of an acquired or metabolic cause for encephalopathy
